newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Sihanouk pardons killers of American woman.
newsitem.headline: Sihanouk pardons killers of American woman.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk on Thursday met the wish of an American academic by granting an amnesty to two men jailed for murdering his wife last year.

"I shall grant the two prisoners the amnesty requested by you," Sihanouk wrote to James Hadden, whose wife Susan and a guide were shot dead while travelling by car to a remote temple in the northwest province of Siem Reap in January 1995.

The king's letter was released by the royal palace, along with a September 8 letter from Hadden to Sihanouk and a copy of the king's letter asking Justice Minister Chem Snguon to prepare a royal decree granting amnesty to Kang Chleu and Sok Khok.

A provincial court in August last year convicted the two former Khmer Rouge guerrillas of taking part in the killing and sentenced them to jail terms of between 15 and 18 years. They confessed only to robbing the Haddens.
Two alleged accomplices were sentenced to 20 years imprisonment in absentia.
James Hadden sought a royal pardon in a September 8 letter to Sihanouk from his Texas home.
Hadden wrote that the knowledge the two men would spend years in jail with no hope of rehabilitation was a source of great distress to him.

He reiterated remarks made in his statement to the trial of the two men, saying his family did not seek revenge but wanted only to see the gap between rich and poor shrink in Cambodia so that the likelihood of such a robbery and crime would lessen.

"I hope that you will agree to release Khang Chleun and Sok Khok as part of the amnesty for Mr. Ieng Sary and his Khmer Rouge faction," Hadden wrote in reference to a royal pardon granted last month to the leader of dissident Khmer Rouge guerrillas.

Ieng Sary, who broke with Khmer Rouge hardliners in August and is negotiating peace with the government, was sentenced to death in absentia for his role in the deaths of more than a million people as foreign minister in the 1975-79 Khmer Rouge regime.
